entry.title: 🏢 Building taxonomy
entry.subtitle: Simplified building taxonomy of selected cities
entry.excerpt: A minimalist small-multiple grid visualizing the 100 most geometrically complex buildings in each city, computed from OpenStreetMap building geometries.
entry.content:
## Introduction Plot simplified taxonomies of buildings across selected cities using PyData, QuackOSM and Metaflow. > **[#30DayMapChallenge | Day 3: Polygons | 2024](https://30daymapchallenge.com/)** (see: ["30DayMapChallenge" official Github repo ](https://github.com/tjukanovt/30DayMapChallenge)) > > Recently I saw a post by Daniel Gorokhov who illustrated building taxonomy of "interesting buildings" in Milano, Italy, Stockholm, Sweden and Amsterdam, Nethedlands. Here is my extension for that post, with some more cities, mostly in USA, but also in Europe. > >

Chart type is "small multiple" (a.k.a. "grid chart"). How was it made? I run a script that loaded all mapped buildings within city area and counted exterior vertices (nodes) for all of them. Still, I did not explicitly count inner polygons, like courtyards or patios. Then, I took one hundred of buildings with the most nodes to plot them.

> >

> > --- > Made with #Python > Data: #OSM, #OpenStreetMap retrieved with [QuackOSM ](https://kraina-ai.github.io/quackosm/0.12.0/examples/advanced_examples/osm_extracts/#query-osm-extract-by-name) > #dataviz #datavisualization **Inspiration:** ["building taxonomy of Milano, Stockholm and Amsterdam" ](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/daniel-gorokhov_30daymapchallenge-geospatial-maps-activity-7259234326775521280-melE?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) by [Daniel Gorokhov ](https://thisisdaniel.co/) **Further works:** ["Visualizing a building shapes taxonomy - The City Summit 🏙️🗻 project" ](https://kamilraczycki.com/blog/City-Summit) by [Kamil Raczycki ](https://kamilraczycki.com/) ## Method ? The chart is a **small multiple** (grid chart): - Extract all mapped buildings within each city boundary. - Count exterior vertices (nodes) for each building polygon (inner courtyards/patios not explicitly counted). - Plot the 100 buildings with the most nodes. Key caveats: 1. Under this methodology, “interesting” buildings can be repetitive due to construction patterns (housing projects, industrial structures, etc.). 2.
